idea: MpcFirewall eliminates the 32-byte blind-signing vulnerability in NEAR Chain Signatures (v1.signer). Existing NEAR agent-security tools rely on Function Call Keys, which only inspect NEAR-native calls and are completely blind when an agent passes an opaque 32-byte keccak256 digest to v1.signer to sign Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, or Bitcoin transactions—allowing a compromised agent to disguise ERC20.approve(drainer, MaxUint256) or nested multicall drains behind a valid Function Call Key. MpcFirewall solves this by owning the MPC derivation path inside a Rust NEAR smart contract (contracts/mpc-firewall): agents must submit raw unsigned EVM EIP-1559/Legacy RLP bytes or raw Bitcoin tx bytes instead of hashes. The contract decodes RLP and ABI calldata recursively on-chain (catching unlimited approvals, setApprovalForAll, disallowed chainIds, and smuggled multicall drains), computes keccak256/sha256d on-chain, enforces autonomous caps, escalates oversized valid txs to Trezu/SputnikDAO multisig proposals, and runs confidential intent-vs-calldata risk checks inside NEAR AI Cloud TEE.
